sections.h2: Which offices run property tax in Flagler?
sections.html:
In Flagler the Property Appraiser sets value. The Tax Collector sends notices and takes payment. Millage is set by the levying bodies: county commissioners, the school board, city commissions and others.

The Tax Collector's website, flaglertax.gov, has pages for property taxes, tangible personal property tax, tourist development tax, business tax receipts and veteran benefits. For questions about a value, an exemption or a classification, contact the Flagler County Property Appraiser directly and ask for the current forms and filing dates. Deeds are recorded, and foreclosure and tax deed auctions are run, by the circuit court clerk.

sections.h2: How are Flagler County property taxes billed?
sections.html:
Flagler bills after the year ends, and notices land around the start of November. The Tax Collector explains that the tax year runs January 1 to December 31 and payment begins November 1 of that year, and its homepage notes that real estate and tangible personal property bills are mailed October 31.

The process runs in a set order:

  • The Property Appraiser establishes values and applies exemptions to complete the tax roll.
  • The certified roll goes to the Tax Collector.
  • The Tax Collector merges in non-ad valorem assessments, which are set amounts that do not depend on value and appear on the same notice.
  • The notice is mailed to the owner's last address on the roll.

If a mortgage servicer pays from escrow, the servicer can request the bill under criteria set by the Tax Collector, and the owner gets a copy for information.

sections.h2: What else does the Flagler Tax Collector handle for property owners?
sections.html:
Beyond the real estate bill, the office runs several accounts that matter to landlords and sellers who own rental or business property. Its website lists these as separate service pages.

  • Tangible personal property tax, which applies to furnishings and equipment used in a rental or business.
  • Tourist development tax, owed on short stays in a rental.
  • Business tax receipts for operating a business in the county.
  • Veteran benefits information.
  • Online payments for tax bills.

An owner closing out a rental should ask the office to confirm that each of these accounts is current and closed, because a balance on one can surface long after the deed records. The same counter also handles driver license and vehicle registration work. Plates on passenger cars and similar vehicles expire at midnight on the owner's birthday, which is a useful reminder when you update your address after a move.

If you cannot visit in person, use the online payment page rather than a link from a text or email. The office has warned that fraudulent texts are circulating in the state agency's name.

sections.h2: What if a Flagler tax bill never arrives?
sections.html:
Nonreceipt is no defense. The Tax Collector cites section 197.122, which tells owners to learn the amount due and pay before delinquency, mailed bill or not.

This catches sellers who moved out, landlords whose tenants get the mail and heirs at a house with an outdated address. The Tax Collector's lobbies may close at 4 p.m. when crowded, and the office warns about text messages that falsely claim to come from the state motor vehicle agency, so check the account yourself on the official site.

sections.h2: What dates drive the Flagler tax year?
sections.html:
Florida's statewide calendar runs here, and Flagler's offices carry out each step.

Calendar steps from the Florida Department of Revenue taxpayer page
DateStep
January 1Assessment date
March 1Exemption filings due
April 1Tangible personal property returns
AugustProposed-tax notice mailed
25 days after the noticeValue petition window
September and OctoberMillage hearings
NovemberBills and early-payment discount
April 1 followingDelinquent

The early-payment discount falls month by month, from 4 percent for a November payment down to 1 percent in February.

sections.h2: Can Flagler owners pay in installments or defer?
sections.html:
Both options exist, and the Tax Collector takes the requests. Installment requests are due on May 1 during the assessment year, and a deferral request on Form DR-570 is due March 31 after it.

Deferral lets a homestead owner postpone the part of the bill that exceeds a share of household income. The share is 5 percent for most owners and 3 percent for a permanent resident 65 or older. Partial payments before delinquency are accepted only if the Tax Collector chooses to take them. Ask how Flagler handles an installment plan before you plan around it, since the May deadline falls well before bills are mailed.

sections.h2: Does my Flagler assessment cap follow the house to a buyer?
sections.html:
The new owner starts at full just value. The seller's capped assessment does not transfer, because a change of title resets the parcel the next January, with exceptions such as spousal transfers.

While a homestead is held, the yearly assessed increase stops at the lower of 3 percent or inflation. DOR's chart prints 2.7 percent for 2026. Sellers moving inside Florida can port part of that benefit to a new home if they claim it within three years. Both forms reach the Property Appraiser by that same March 1 deadline.

sections.h2: Which veteran breaks can Flagler County owners ask about?
sections.html:
The Tax Collector's site has a veteran benefits page, and the Property Appraiser handles the exemptions themselves. Florida's list is short.

  • A $5,000 cut in assessed value for a disabled ex-servicemember rated 10 percent or more.
  • A homestead discount tied to the VA rating for a veteran 65 or older with a permanent service-connected disability.
  • A deployment-based exemption on Form DR-501M.

Ask the Property Appraiser what proof each one needs, and bring discharge or VA rating papers to that conversation.

sections.h2: What if a Flagler County parcel reaches a tax deed auction?
sections.html:
After a certificate has aged two years, its holder may ask for a deed, and the clerk then auctions the parcel publicly. The tax collector assembles the notice list: titleholder, mortgagees, lienholders, the assessed party and any recorded contract buyer.

  • The top bidder leaves a nonrefundable deposit, set at the larger of 5 percent of the bid or $200.
  • The balance, stamps and recording costs are due inside 24 hours, excluding weekends and holidays.
  • An unsold parcel joins the county's lands-available list.

An owner who sells ahead of the auction can redeem from proceeds. Ask the Flagler Tax Collector for a redemption figure, since interest makes it move.

sections.h2: What happens to a Flagler tax bill at closing?
sections.html:
Closing agents confirm the account and pay what is owed from the seller's proceeds. Get the parcel balance from the Tax Collector's office. The clerk collects deed stamps at recording, at a statewide rate of 70 cents on each $100 of price.

A parcel with a certificate attached can still be sold. Settle the certificate at the table so the buyer gets a clean title.

faqs.q: When does Flagler County mail property tax bills?
faqs.a: Around the start of November. The Tax Collector's site says real estate and tangible personal property bills are mailed October 31, and payment begins November 1.

faqs.q: What if I never receive my Flagler County tax bill?
faqs.a: You still owe the tax. Section 197.122 puts the duty on the owner to find out the amount and pay before the delinquency date, so contact the Tax Collector and the Property Appraiser.

faqs.q: Can I defer Flagler County property tax?
faqs.a: A homestead owner can apply on Form DR-570 by March 31 after the assessment year. Deferral covers tax above 5 percent of household income, or 3 percent for a permanent resident 65 or older.

faqs.q: Does my homestead cap transfer to the buyer of my Flagler County house?
faqs.a: No. A sale resets the property to just value the next January 1. You may be able to port part of your cap to a new Florida homestead.

faqs.q: Who sets Flagler County millage rates?
faqs.a: The levying bodies do: county commissioners, the school board, city commissions and other authorities. The Property Appraiser sets value, not the rate.
